market_rationale: Macro backdrop is a hawkish-tightening regime: Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September, 10y at 5.29%, 30y at 5.64%, core PCE 3.0% and headline 3.4% with projections implying another hike by year-end. Breadth is poor (RSP -4.5% vs SPY over 21 sessions, only 26% of assets positive), duration and credit are falling, the dollar is rising, and leadership is extremely narrow in semis/tech. Cross-sectional dispersion is high, but the recent losers are mostly rate-sensitive or commodity exposures with weak prior trends, so their declines read as fundamentally driven rather than overreaction. With an FOMC on Oct 27-28, CPI mid-month, and a jobs report Oct 2 inside the window, I see limited strong reversal edge and prefer the cap-weighted benchmark or quality large-cap exposure.
portfolio_rationale: Only LARGE_VALUE qualifies as a plausible overreaction with a quality prior trend and low volatility, but its edge is marginal (54%) and falls below the 55% eligibility bar, so the deterministic rule should default to SPY. Shock-reversal candidates (metals, silver, solar, defense, South Africa) show prolonged negative prior trends consistent with fundamental pressure from higher real rates and a stronger dollar, not transient overreaction. Strength lanes (semis, Taiwan, cyber) have real prior support but are extended and highly volatile into a hawkish FOMC and CPI window, offering no reliable excess return. Bond dislocations reflect genuine repricing of the policy path.
